title: As a developer, I can submit a local audio or video file for transcription through a documented API endpoint, with accepted formats and size limits published
As a developer, I can pass a public or signed URL and the service fetches and transcribes the recording without my uploading it
As a developer, multi-hour recordings are accepted in a single job, with the maximum duration and file size documented
As a developer, I can run many transcription jobs in parallel, with concurrency limits and queueing behavior documented
As a developer, I can choose among documented transcription models with published accuracy, latency, and cost tradeoffs
As a founder, published accuracy claims come with a methodology or benchmark dataset I can check, not bare marketing numbers
As a developer, I can boost domain terms, names, and jargon through custom vocabulary or keyword boosting so they transcribe correctly
As a developer, transcripts come back with punctuation, casing, and number formatting applied, and I can turn the formatting off
As a developer, I create a transcription job and poll its status through documented job states until the result is ready
As a developer, a webhook or callback fires when a job completes or fails, so nothing in my system has to poll
As a developer, failed jobs return documented error codes with retry guidance, and a bad file fails fast instead of hanging
As a developer, I can attach my own identifiers or metadata to a job and get them back in results and webhook payloads
As a developer, I can request speaker diarization and the transcript labels who said what
As a developer, stereo or multichannel recordings can be transcribed per channel, so each side of a call stays separate
As a developer, I can get word-level timestamps so every word maps to its position in the recording
As a developer, results come back as structured JSON with utterances or segments and confidence values, not just a text blob
As a developer, I can export a transcript as SRT or VTT captions through the API or a documented path
As a developer, I can stream live audio over a documented WebSocket or streaming endpoint and receive transcription in real time
As a developer, streaming results distinguish interim from final transcripts, with the finality semantics documented
As a developer, the supported languages are published as a concrete list, with any per-model or per-feature differences stated
As a developer, the service can detect the spoken language automatically instead of requiring me to declare it
As a developer, I can get a transcript translated to another language through a documented option or endpoint

As an AI-native user, an agent holding an API key can take a recording from submission to finished transcript (auth, job creation, result retrieval) from the public docs alone, with no human step in between
As an AI-native user, an agent can compute the cost of a transcription job before submitting it, because pricing is published per audio minute or hour with add-on prices itemized
